text:
maya: pushed the audit-sampling egress tighten to apac-prod at 09:12 UTC to meet the new retention policy. seeing provisioning failures for new GPU nodes. raising since this impacts capacity :warning:

jon: what errors are we seeing on the nodes?

maya: init logs show repeated KMS decrypt failures during instance bootstrap, then kubelet fails join. snippet:
```
2026-03-20T09:14:03Z keystore: decrypt failed status=403 message=AccessDenied
2026-03-20T09:14:04Z node-init: connection to keystore.internal.redwood.svc:443 timed out
2026-03-20T09:14:12Z kubelet: node join failed, cert fetch error
```

priya: that aligns with the egress rule we pushed. we are blocking privatelink endpoints used by keystore/metadata.

linh: do we have a quick allowlist we can add? which CIDRs/endpoints to permit?

maya: keystore sits behind privatelink at 10.22.8.0/24 (apac-keystore-privnet). also need access to kms.amazonaws.com and sts in the region for cert bootstrap.

omar: temporary mitigation options:
- rollback the firewall change (fastest)
- add allowlist for 10.22.8.0/24 + 54.239.0.0/16 (aws STS/KMS ranges)
- route node bootstrap via bastion/proxy with egress allowed (costly and slower)

jon: rollback first, then we can incrementally tighten with a canary. rollback window?

maya: can rollback now. question: we tightened sampling to drop some audit packets, security asked for the change yesterday (ticket SEC-4521). will rollback break compliance posture?

priya: short rollback (<=1h) is acceptable if we capture packet/header samples and store them externally for SEC audit. we need to preserve the dropped samples for the last 3 hours.

taylor: cost impact if we route through hosted fallback while fixing: estimate ~ $2.1k/day if we proxy all bootstrap traffic through our hosted egress NATs.

linh: can we do selective allowlist for only node bootstrap IPs (warmpool nodes) instead of full aws ranges? that limits blast radius and reduces cost.

omar: yes — we can add warmpool CIDR 10.40.0.0/22 and the keystore privatelink CIDR as exceptions. that should restore new node bootstraps within ~5m after rules apply.

deploy-bot: deploy 8570-audit-sample-ephemeral (maya) started at 09:12:18 UTC -> changed firewall ACLs in apac-prod

maya: I'll flip the rule to add the two allowlist CIDRs then monitor node bootstrap. doing change now (09:20 UTC).

sre-oncall: when you flip, run a small canary: request 3 nodes from warmpool-apac-canary, wait for kubelet joins, run a 1GB inference workload to validate keystore decrypts KV cache. post result here.

maya: change applied at 09:22 UTC, ACL updated:
```
allow 10.40.0.0/22 -> egress:keystore (apac)
allow 10.22.8.0/24 -> privatelink-keystore
```

maya: warmpool canary triggered (3 nodes) 09:24 UTC

jon: canary nodes joined at 09:27 UTC, kubelet healthy. keystore decrypts succeeded. :thumbsup:

priya: SEC: please attach the preserved audit snapshots from 06:00-09:30 to SEC-4521. we need those for post-mortem.

linh: small follow-ups:
- add a targeted infra change to update the firewall automation to accept an allowlist variable for warmpool bootstrap IPs
- add automated test in staging that runs e2e keystore decrypt during firewall rule change CI

omar: created infra PR #2497 to add allowlist var and a rollback playbook. assigning to maya for validation.

taylor: note on costs: if we leave the full aws range open it increases NAT egress bill significantly. prefer targeted CIDRs.

maya: will raise a post-change review doc with timeline and impact metrics (node failures, time-to-provision, added cost). planning to keep the relaxed allowlist until next deploy window unless SEC requests otherwise.

sre-oncall: marking incident INC-20263, will keep watch on capacity metrics for next 6 hours and notify if warm pool < 85% ready.

maya: thanks all. I'll attach logs and the canary runbook to INC-20263 and close once SEC confirms preserved audit data has been ingested. :white_check_mark:
